SETUP GUIDE

## Connect Spotify MCP Tool with your Agent

TypeScriptPython

1

#### Install Composio

typescript

Copy

```typescript
npm install @composio/core ai @ai-sdk/mcp @ai-sdk/openai
```

Install the Composio SDK and your agent framework

2

#### Create a session with MCP enabled

typescript

Copy

```typescript
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio();
const { mcp } = await composio.create("your-user-id", {
  toolkits: ["spotify"],
  mcp: true,
});
```

Create a session scoped to Spotify and read its MCP URL and headers

3

#### Connect your agent to the MCP server

typescript

Copy

```typescript
import { createMCPClient } from "@ai-sdk/mcp";
import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";
import { generateText, stepCountIs } from "ai";

const client = await createMCPClient({
  transport: { type: "http", url: mcp.url, headers: mcp.headers },
});

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: openai("gpt-5.6-sol"),
  tools: await client.tools(),
  prompt: "Add my top tracks to a new playlist called Summer Vibes",
  stopWhen: stepCountIs(10),
});

console.log(text);
await client.close();
```

Pass the session's MCP URL and headers to your agent and run a Spotify request

SETUP GUIDE

## Connect Spotify API Tool with your Agent

TypeScriptPython

1

#### Install Composio

typescript

Copy

```typescript
npm install @composio/core @composio/openai openai
```

Install the Composio SDK, the OpenAI provider, and the OpenAI SDK

2

#### Create a Composio session

typescript

Copy

```typescript
import OpenAI from "openai";
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";
import { OpenAIResponsesProvider } from "@composio/openai";

const composio = new Composio({ provider: new OpenAIResponsesProvider() });
const client = new OpenAI();

const session = await composio.create("your-user-id", { toolkits: ["spotify"] });
const tools = await session.tools();
```

Initialize Composio with the OpenAI Responses provider and create a session scoped to Spotify

3

#### Run Spotify tools with your agent

typescript

Copy

```typescript
let response = await client.responses.create({
  model: "gpt-5.6-sol",
  tools,
  input: [{ role: "user", content: "Add my top tracks to a new playlist called Summer Vibes" }],
});

while (response.output.some((o) => o.type === "function_call")) {
  const outputs = await composio.provider.handleToolCalls(session, response.output);
  response = await client.responses.create({
    model: "gpt-5.6-sol",
    tools,
    previous_response_id: response.id,
    input: outputs,
  });
}

console.log(response.output_text);
```

Send a request, execute the Spotify tool calls through the session, and print the final answer

## Why Use Composio?

### AI Native Spotify Integration

- Supports both Spotify MCP and direct API based integrations
- Structured, LLM-friendly schemas for reliable tool execution
- Rich coverage for searching, playing, and managing your Spotify music and podcasts

### Managed Auth

- Built-in OAuth handling with automatic token refresh and rotation
- Central place to manage, scope, and revoke Spotify access
- Per user and per environment credentials instead of hard-coded keys

### Agent Optimized Design

- Tools are tuned using real error and success rates to improve reliability over time
- Comprehensive execution logs so you always know what ran, when, and on whose behalf

### Enterprise Grade Security

- Fine-grained RBAC so you control which agents and users can access Spotify
- Scoped, least privilege access to Spotify resources
- Full audit trail of agent actions to support review and compliance

FAQ

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need my own Spotify developer credentials or OAuth app?+

Spotify requires connections to go through your own OAuth app. You register it once with Spotify, add its client ID and secret in the Composio dashboard, and from then on everyone connects by signing in to Spotify as usual. Composio handles the rest of the flow and the token refresh.

### Can I use multiple toolkits together?+

Yes! Composio's Tool Router enables agents to use multiple toolkits. [Learn more](https://docs.composio.dev/tool-router/overview).

### Is Composio secure with my Spotify account?+

Yes. Composio is SOC 2 Type II compliant and is built to keep your Spotify connection and credentials secure. OAuth tokens and API keys are encrypted, and sensitive customer data is protected at rest and in transit.

Composio also undergoes independent security testing and continuously monitors its systems for security threats. You can review the latest reports and policies in the [Composio Trust Center](https://trust.composio.dev/).

### What if the API changes?+

Composio maintains and updates all toolkit integrations automatically, so your agents always work with the latest API versions.

### Does the agent act as me inside Spotify?+

When you connect a Spotify account through Composio, every action runs under that account, so anything the agent creates, sends, or changes shows up in Spotify as done by you. Keep an approval step in your prompt for actions with side effects, such as sending or deleting, and have the agent draft first.

### Which Spotify permissions does Composio get?+

Exactly the ones Spotify lists on its consent screen when you connect. Review that screen before approving. If you connect a work account, your Spotify administrator may need to approve the app first, and you can revoke the access inside Spotify whenever you want.

### Can I use multiple Spotify accounts with Claude and ChatGPT?+

Yes. Composio supports multiple connected accounts for the same app, and that works in Claude, ChatGPT, or any other assistant you connect through Composio. Give each Spotify connection a name such as work or personal, and the assistant uses the one you mention in the request. Each account keeps its own credentials and nothing is merged.

### What happens when my Spotify access expires or I revoke it?+

Composio refreshes Spotify tokens automatically, so day to day you do nothing. If you revoke access inside Spotify, or Spotify invalidates the session, the connection shows as expired in Composio and the agent stops acting on that account until you reconnect it, which is a single sign-in.

### Does using Spotify through Composio cost extra?+

Composio's free Hobby plan includes 100,000 tool calls per month with no credit card, which covers most personal Spotify use. Paid plans add higher limits and team features. Your Spotify plan and its API limits still apply as usual.

### How is Composio different from the Spotify connectors already built into Claude and ChatGPT?+

Built-in connectors usually give one AI access to a limited set of apps. Many people use Composio because it lets their AI connect to more apps than it normally supports, or connect to multiple accounts for the same app (e.g. connect Claude to multiple Spotify accounts).

With Composio, you connect Spotify once and then use it across different AI assistants without setting it up separately in each one. Connect your apps to Composio once, then connect Composio to whichever AI you use, whether that's Claude, ChatGPT, Hermes, or your own custom assistant.
